intro: In these questions the signs of an equation are hidden, coded or mixed up. You choose the signs (or the swap) that make the equation true. Everything depends on working it out in the right order: BODMAS.

tips.title: BODMAS: the order to work it out
tips.body:
BODMAS tells you what to do first.
B – Brackets: ( ) first, then { }, then [ ].
O – Of and powers: ½ of 10 = 5, and 3² = 9.
D and M – Division ÷ and Multiplication ×, from left to right.
A and S – Addition + and Subtraction −, from left to right.
D and M are equal, so do whichever comes first from the left; the same goes for A and S.
In the picture, 12 + 12 − 12 ÷ 12 − 12: first 12 ÷ 12 = 1, which leaves 12 + 12 − 1 − 12 = 11.
With brackets: 10 + (6 − 2) × 3 ÷ 2 = 10 + 4 × 3 ÷ 2 = 10 + 12 ÷ 2 = 10 + 6 = 16.
tips.caption: BODMAS: brackets, then of, then ÷ and ×, then + and −.

tips.title: Try the options one by one
tips.body: Put each option's signs into the * places in order and work the equation out. Look at the answer's size first: much bigger than the numbers means a × is needed; much smaller means ÷ or −. That rules out some options straight away.

tips.title: Letters or shapes for signs
tips.body: When K means +, L means × and so on, first write the equation again with the real signs, and only then work it out. 50 K 40 L 30 M 20 N 10 becomes 50 + 40 × 30 ÷ 20 − 10 = 50 + 60 − 10 = 100.

tips.title: Signs with changed meanings
tips.body:
Example: + means ÷, × means +, − means × and ÷ means −.
1. Write the code as a key first: + → ÷   × → +   − → ×   ÷ → −
2. Copy the option onto a new line, changing each sign as you copy it, by looking at the key. Never change the signs in the original line.
3. Now work out the new line with BODMAS.
{(19 × 11) + 15} ÷ 2 becomes {(19 + 11) ÷ 15} − 2 = 2 − 2 = 0.
The trap: changing one sign at a time in the same line. Change × to + and you get {(19 + 11) + 15} ÷ 2. Then, when you change + to ÷, the + that was a × gets changed a second time: {(19 ÷ 11) ÷ 15} ÷ 2. That is wrong.
If you still mix them up, first write A, B, C, D in place of the signs, then turn each letter into its new sign.

tips.title: Swapping two signs or two numbers
tips.body: Swap the two signs (or numbers) in the equation, work out the left side and compare it with the right side. In 12 + 3 × 5 ÷ 5 − 1 = 36, swap × and +: 12 × 3 + 5 ÷ 5 − 1 = 36 + 1 − 1 = 36.
